title: Migrating between engines: what always breaks

videos.script: A migration between engines looks like a copy. Read the rows out of one server and write them into the other. {{copy}} The rows are the easy part. What breaks is what they mean. A date made of zeros, which PostgreSQL has no word for. A yes-or-no flag that holds the number two. An e-mail address that MySQL compared without caring about case, and PostgreSQL compares exactly. {{breaks}} In this lesson you install MySQL beside PostgreSQL, on the same machine, and give it a small database with all of those habits. {{mysql}} Then you move it with pgloader. It stops three times. Twice the problem is the tool, and once it is the data. {{pgloader}} When it finally finishes, it says it moved every row. You check that yourself, with a count and a checksum on each side. {{checksum}} One table disagrees. Finding out why is the most useful part of the lesson, because the answer is a decision nobody wrote down. {{decision}} And at the end comes the part no tool moves: the application, which is still speaking MySQL. {{application}}
